subtype: Approach: adjusting after the first month in the new city [Revision]
passage: Sit down, and I'll tell you about my first flat in Bengaluru, because I got it wrong. I am Sachin. I had signed a lease in a lovely colony after one visit on a Sunday, when the roads were empty. On the first Monday, the drive to the office took an hour and a half. Six weeks in, I was so tired that I was snapping at my wife Uma over nothing. One night I finally said to myself: I chose with half the facts. There was a penalty for leaving the lease. I paid it anyway and moved to a flat ten minutes from the office. Uma called it the best money we ever wasted. My first choice was not stupid, beta. It was made with what I knew then.

qa.q: How long did the drive take on the first Monday?
qa.a: It took an hour and a half.

qa.q: What was Sachin feeling six weeks in?
qa.a: Sachin felt exhausted and irritable, shown by snapping at Uma over nothing.

qa.q: What choice did Sachin make at the turning point, and what did it cost?
qa.a: Sachin paid the lease penalty and moved to a flat ten minutes from the office, which cost money but saved daily time and mood.

qa.q: How did Uma see the move?
qa.a: Uma called it the best money they ever wasted, which shows relief that the tiredness eased.

grounding: Sachin recalls moving to a flat closer to work despite a lease penalty, after seeing the first choice was made with limited information.
